items.headline: Diner says table given away after hour-long wait at Rowley's
items.text:
Very disappointing experience and extremely poor customer service.

When I arrived, I was informed that the waiting time would be approximately 30–35 minutes. After waiting for that period, I followed up with the employee, only to be told that I needed to wait another 30 minutes.

After waiting for a full hour, I approached the staff again, and to my surprise, they simply apologized and told me that someone else had taken my place!

What makes this situation even more unacceptable is that nobody called me, contacted me, or informed me that my turn had come. Apparently, the staff simply called out a name, and someone else took my place, despite the fact that I had been sitting right next to the employee the entire time and had never left the waiting area.

Furthermore, I was receiving WhatsApp updates showing my waiting time, so there was a clear system in place to track the queue. How could my place be given to someone else without any proper notification or communication?

This clearly reflects a serious lack of organization, professionalism, communication, and respect for customers’ time.

It is completely unacceptable to keep a customer waiting for an entire hour, fail to notify them when their turn comes, and then casually apologize because someone else has taken their place.

I am requesting that management personally investigate this incident, review the queue records and WhatsApp notification history, and explain how my place was given to someone else without properly contacting me. I also expect management to take corrective action, ensure staff follow a clear and fair queue management process, and implement a proper notification and confirmation system so that this does not happen to other customers.

I would appreciate a direct response from management explaining what went wrong and what specific steps will be taken to prevent this from happening again. A simple apology is not enough when customers’ time is wasted due to poor organization.

A very frustrating and disappointing experience. Completely unacceptable!

items.headline: Diner calls Rowley's overrated, says steak and sauces disappointed
items.text:
First time trying Rowley's in Abu Dhabi, and my final verdict? Overrated. Period.😅

I've tried quite a few steakhouses around the UAE, and personally, I feel there are plenty of better options. Even Entrecôte at Yas Mall, for example, is far superior in terms of taste. Sorry, but the flavours at Rowley's just didn't work for me.

We tried the different sauces, and honestly, none really stood out. The Best Sauce reminded me of ketchup mixed with chilli. The Secret Sauce was nice, but nothing that made me say wow. As for the Special Sauce, it tasted like another version of peppercorn sauce.

Steak-wise, I actually preferred the Signature Ribeye over the Wagyu. It was the better choice for me.

On the positive side, the ambience was marvellous, and the service was excellent. A special mention to Miss Thandar, who was absolutely superb. She really made us feel welcome and deserves recognition for her hospitality.

Overall, a beautiful restaurant with fantastic service, but unfortunately, the food didn't live up to the hype for me. Perhaps my expectations were too high after hearing so much about Rowley's.

Would I come back? Probably not for the steak. There are simply too many other steakhouses in the UAE that I personally enjoy more.
items.author: AZ BEAN

items.headline: Diner says souvlaki took 40 minutes amid cold, inattentive service
items.text:
One of the worst restaurant experiences I’ve had in the UAE. Extremely disappointing.

I’ve lived in the UAE long enough to know that customer service here is generally exceptional. In almost every restaurant, staff are welcoming, polite, and attentive. Unfortunately, my experience at EVA was the complete opposite.

While I wouldn’t describe the staff as outright rude, the service was incredibly cold, inattentive, and unprofessional. One waiter in particular made the entire experience extremely unpleasant. At times, I genuinely felt that some of the delays and mistakes were deliberate, although I obviously cannot know that for certain.

We placed an order for two items, but only one arrived. At another point, I watched a waiter receive our plate from a colleague and leave it sitting there for approximately two minutes while chatting with other staff before finally bringing it to our table.

As for the food, I ordered a simple portion of chicken souvlaki, without any sides, salad, or fries. It took over 40 minutes to arrive. To make matters worse, it didn’t even come with a small piece of bread.

When we asked for some bread for our 16-month-old daughter, simply so she could have something to hold and nibble on while we ate, we were told we would be charged for it. I don’t expect everything to be free, but a little hospitality and common sense would have gone a long way.

The bread never arrived while we were eating. In fact, after waiting around 15 minutes, it was finally brought to us while I was already paying the bill!

Even getting the bill was unnecessarily frustrating. After another long wait, I eventually had to get up, walk to the cashier, and ask to pay there because I simply wanted to leave.

And unfortunately, the food itself did absolutely nothing to compensate for the terrible service. Nothing we tried was particularly impressive, and I’ve had far better and more authentic Greek food at other restaurants in the UAE.

I rarely leave negative reviews. In fact, I much prefer taking the time to recognize businesses that provide great food and service. But this experience was so disappointing that I felt it deserved to be shared.

I sincerely hope someone from the management team reads this and takes it seriously. There are some fundamental issues with the service, professionalism, and overall dining experience that need attention.

Poor service, excessive waiting times, disappointing food, and absolutely no sense of Greek hospitality.

I would not recommend EVA, and I certainly won’t be returning.

items.headline: Diner waited an hour as hostess's acquaintances skipped the queue
items.text:
The food was delicious, but unfortunately, the overall experience was disappointing.

We waited for an hour to be seated, while we noticed several customers arriving after us being allowed in without waiting simply because they knew the hostess. This was extremely unfair and unprofessional.

When we were finally seated, our table was surrounded by men. We requested to move to the family section, but our request was refused despite several empty tables being available. Surprisingly, they only agreed to change our table after I mentioned that I would be sharing my experience on Google Reviews. It shouldn’t take the mention of a negative review for a customer’s reasonable request to be accommodated.

We ordered the Short Ribs and Pepperoni pizzas, and both were absolutely delicious.

It’s a shame that such excellent food is overshadowed by poor customer service and preferential treatment. All customers deserve the same level of respect and service, regardless of whether they know the staff or not.

items.headline: Diner calls Power Lunch misleading, goes to McDonald's after
items.text:
Honestly, this was one of the worst steakhouse experiences I've ever had. I walked in expecting a decent meal, but walked out feeling like I'd been traumatized by the entire dining experience.

Let's start with the food. The salad was absolutely pathetic, the steak was nothing special (just basic and underwhelming), and the gravy was ridiculously salty.

Even the complimentary drinks served outside somehow managed to add to the trauma. At this point, I don't even know what to say anymore.

But what really made the experience worse was the so-called Power Lunch. Apparently, it's only available Monday to Friday, yet this restriction was nowhere clearly mentioned in their menu or advertised offer. That's seriously misleading. I genuinely felt scammed by the advertisement.

And here's the best part: after paying for and eating at a steakhouse, we actually ended up going straight to McDonald's because we were still unsatisfied.

To be fair, the servers were friendly and polite. They even asked us to leave a review, and well, here it is. Sorry, guys, but this is my honest feedback. Food-related misleading promotions and disappointing dining experiences shouldn't be normalized.

I've learned a good life lesson today:
"If it's too good to be true, it probably isn't true."

Imagine leaving a steakhouse and needing McDonald's to complete your meal!

Save your money and manage your expectations. You've been warned!⚠️⚠️⚠️

items.headline: Cold welcome, small portions and loud music disappoint diner
items.text:
I rarely write negative reviews, and my intention here is not simply to criticise but to offer constructive feedback that might encourage the owners to improve the standards and reputation of their brand.

The restaurant certainly makes an impressive first impression. The building is beautiful, with striking architecture, luxurious décor, and ample parking. Clearly, considerable investment has gone into creating an attractive venue. Unfortunately, the quality of hospitality, service, and overall dining experience falls well short of what the surroundings promise.

First, the welcome. Upon arrival, the lady behind the reception monitor immediately began taking our details without a smile, a warm greeting, or any attempt to make us feel welcome. It felt more like checking into an administrative office than entering a premium restaurant.

Second, the seating arrangements. Without asking about our preferences or the purpose of our visit, we were escorted to a rather intimate, romantic seating area. I was dining with a female colleague, and the arrangement felt inappropriate and somewhat embarrassing. A simple question about seating preferences would have avoided this uncomfortable situation.

Third, the management and service. The manager approached our table and delivered what sounded like a rehearsed speech about the food, including an explanation of why a particular type of bread is placed beneath the kebab. There was no attempt to establish a conversation, engage with us, or understand our experience. Hospitality should be a dialogue, not a recorded presentation. Why I felt I am facing a robot rather than an experienced manager.

When I mentioned that my experience at the brand’s London restaurant had been rather different, he immediately insisted that both establishments were 100% identical. Rather than listening to a customer’s observation, he chose to contradict it. This is particularly concerning for a brand that presumably values consistency and reputation. Brand consistency should be demonstrated through the customer experience, not defended through argument.

Fourth, the food. The portions were disappointingly small, hardly sufficient for one person, particularly given the positioning of the restaurant. The dessert was equally underwhelming in flavour and presentation. While the staff appeared to be trying, enthusiasm alone cannot compensate for inadequate training and a lack of attention to detail. The temperature was cold and no arrangement to keep the food warm why having it or make the temperature a bit comfortable.

Finally, the atmosphere. Perhaps one of the most disappointing aspects was the music. It was excessively loud, with an almost party-like character, completely disconnected from the restaurant’s elegant architecture and supposedly refined dining environment. Combined with the dark and rather cold interior, it created an uncomfortable and confusing atmosphere. We found it difficult to relax and enjoy our meal.

My overall impression: This is a restaurant where substantial money has been invested in the building, interior design, and visual presentation, but seemingly far less attention has been given to the people, training, service culture, and actual dining experience.

Luxury is not defined by expensive decorations. It is defined by how customers are welcomed, understood, respected, and looked after.

I genuinely hope the owners take this feedback seriously. The venue has enormous potential, but without better hospitality standards, appropriate staff training, improved food quality, and a more thoughtfully managed atmosphere, the impressive surroundings alone will not sustain the reputation of the brand.

A beautiful restaurant, unfortunately, does not automatically make a good restaurant.
items.author: Ehsan Daneshvar
